depth_preview.title: Depth
depth_preview.description: Check how far away everything is before you make 3D: a 10-second depth clip from where you are on the timeline. Optional.

outputs.o1: A 10-second depth clip you can play beside your source, near is bright and far is dark

tips.t1: Move the playhead to the shot you want to check; the clip starts there.
tips.t2: Higher detail costs more; it is capped at your video's own resolution.
tips.t3: Look for stable depth across a scene — flicker between frames shows up as shimmer in 3D.

stereo_preview.title: 3D look
stereo_preview.description: Per-scene 3D: every scene is measured and classified automatically; adjust the ones that need it, and check a 10-second clip from where you are on the timeline.

outputs.o1: A 10-second 3D clip in the same qualities and formats Make 3D offers
outputs.o2: The per-scene profile computed by the run seeds this page's Auto defaults

tips.t1: Every scene defaults to Auto: the profiler measures how far the action is from the camera and picks one of four shot types — only rows you change are sent as overrides.
tips.t2: Close-up — the subject is near the camera. Depth is kept gentle and the subject pops slightly toward you.
tips.t3: Standard — a mid-distance shot. Balanced depth around the screen plane; the most common case.
tips.t4: Wide — an establishing or far shot. Depth sits behind the screen like a window, which keeps edges clean on shots that are hardest to fill.
tips.t5: Dynamic — the camera or subject distance changes during the scene (push-ins, walk-aways), so the 3D strength adapts across the shot instead of staying fixed.
tips.t6: Override a scene's shot type when the automatic pick reads wrong — e.g. force Close-up on a tight shot the profiler called Standard to make it pop more.
tips.t7: Overall 3D strength scales EVERY scene at once; a per-scene shot-type override wins for its scene.
tips.t8: Edges are Filled by default: the thin gaps that open along object edges in 3D are painted in. The other edge style, Stretched, is under Advanced.
tips.t9: Uncheck “3D” on a scene to ship it as 2D — both eyes identical, no depth (end credits, logos, title cards).
tips.t10: “Profile shots (free)” measures each scene's depth from the preview proxy and seeds the per-scene controls — no charge, about a minute.
tips.t11: Your tweaks persist per project and carry to Make 3D automatically.

production.title: Make 3D
production.description: The whole video (or the part you pick) in 3D. It uses your Depth and 3D look settings and reuses earlier depth work at a discount.

outputs.o1: Your video in every format you pick: Vision Pro spatial video, side by side for other headsets and 3D TVs, red-cyan for a quick check
outputs.o2: Full frame rate at the quality you pick, with Filled edges unless you chose Stretched under Advanced

tips.t1: The summary shows which Depth and 3D look settings this run uses — each can be switched back to automatic.
tips.t2: Reuse is the default: compatible preview artifacts (depth, preprocess) are discounted automatically — the quote shows each reused stage.
tips.t3: Pick “Start from scratch” to recompute everything, e.g. to raise quality beyond what previews ran at.

lifelike_preview.title: Preview
lifelike_preview.description: See a few seconds in 3D before you make the whole video.

outputs.o1: A few seconds of your video in 3D (5 by default), starting at the moment you pick
outputs.o2: Side by side, so you can play it right here (or check it in red-cyan or as a wiggle, free) or on a headset

tips.t1: Pick a moment with the kind of shot that matters most to you — faces, fast motion, or wide views.
tips.t2: A preview costs what the same seconds cost in the final video, with a small minimum per run. Quick look renders half the frame rate for half the price.
tips.t3: Happy with it? Make 3D renders the whole video the same way.
